headline: High: ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files/screenshots while marketingskills can write shared skill files, creating default-path leakage and output-cascade risks.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: ChatGPT Desktop reads uploaded files, screenshots, and supported-app content, so if marketingskills writes prompt-like content into shared skill files, that content can be ingested as instructions. The pair lacks explicit provenance or isolation controls. This is more than manual copy-paste because B can persist content that A may later read.
conditions: IF marketingskills writes attacker-controlled instructions into a file ChatGPT Desktop reads
IF ChatGPT Desktop is pointed at a workspace containing B-authored skill files
mitigations: Restrict ChatGPT Desktop to a separate read-only folder
Remove B write access to any folder A reads
Use a manual review step before A ingests B-authored files
Prefix B files with non-executable templates only
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between shared files and prompts

B_data_leakage.rationale: A touches uploaded files, screenshots, voice, and connected-IDE code, while B can read and write files and call allowlisted network services. If they share a workspace, sensitive content handled by A can be copied into B outputs or transmitted via B's API calls. The profiles do not show isolation, so leakage is plausible in default use.
conditions: IF both agents access the same directory or synced workspace
IF A processes uploaded files or screenshots containing sensitive data
mitigations: Place A and B in separate workspaces
Disable B access to any folder containing A inputs
Review B outputs before external sharing
Delete transient files after each run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A cannot write files, but B can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses. If both operate on the same mutable workspace, B can overwrite artifacts A reads, causing racey or inconsistent state. The conflict is one-sided rather than symmetric, but the shared read/write surface still creates default-path interference.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to use the same writable project directory
IF B modifies files that A later reads
mitigations: Assign distinct working directories
Make A's inputs read-only during B runs
Serialize runs so only one agent mutates files at a time
Snapshot the workspace before B edits it
requires-engineering: add file-locking or orchestration locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: marketingskills explicitly builds on shared context, and ChatGPT Desktop can ingest files and app context. If B consumes A's generated text without verification, A's mistakes can cascade into B's marketing outputs. The profiles do not show a verification gate, so the safer assumption is that A-to-B propagation is possible by default.
conditions: IF B uses A-generated drafts as source material
IF B publishes or forwards outputs without human verification
mitigations: Require a human review before B publishes anything derived from A
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts
Keep source citations alongside generated text
Run a spot-check on factual claims before reuse
requires-engineering: add automated verification between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented for either agent. The main compliance concern is that A handles uploaded files, screenshots, and voice, while B handles marketing context and file-based skills; if regulated data is placed into both, policy alignment is unclear. Because the profiles do not prove a mismatch, this stays low.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into both agents
IF an organizational policy requires documented retention or residency controls
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared workflows
Document which data classes each agent may touch
Review vendor retention settings before use
Keep marketing content free of personal data
requires-engineering: map each agent to a compliance control matrix
